title: Whose cache paid: the realized-versus-ideal prefix-cache term in the cost axis of the HAL leaderboard

glossary.prefix cache: a provider or server keeps the attention states of a prompt prefix so that a later request repeating that prefix pays the cached price $c$ (0.025 to 0.1 of the uncached input price on the two price lists card 2611.22238 cites) for those tokens instead of the full price
glossary.token quadruple $(I_t, R_t, W_t, O_t)$: for model call $t$ of a run: inclusive input tokens, cache-read tokens, cache-write tokens, output tokens, as HAL's trace archive logs them and card 2611.21515 prices them (Eq. 1)
glossary.realized hit share $h^{\\mathrm{real}}_i: $\sum_t R_t / \sum_t I_t$ for run $i$: the share of the run's input tokens the provider actually served from its cache and billed at $c$
glossary.own-cache ideal $h^{\\mathrm{ideal}}_i$: $\sum_t H_t / \sum_t I_t$ with $H_t = \min(P_t, \mathrm{LCP}_t)$, $P_t$ the prompt tokens of call $t$ and $\mathrm{LCP}_t$ its longest common token prefix with call $t-1$ of the same run (card 2611.22238's own-cache accounting): what a token-exact cache with no expiry and no missing breakpoints would have served
glossary.append-only bound $\\bar h_i$: $\sum_t \min(P_t, P_{t-1}) / \sum_t I_t$, computable from token counts alone; equal to the ideal when the scaffold only appends to its prompt, an upper bound otherwise
glossary.cache-plumbing term $g_i$: $h^{\mathrm{ideal}}_i - h^{\mathrm{real}}_i$: the share of the run's input tokens billed at full price that a token-exact cache would have served; it collects breakpoints the scaffold never set, prefixes that expired during tool waits, and provider eviction
glossary.re-priced cost $C^{\\mathrm{ideal}}_i$: the card's Eq. 1 with $R_t$ replaced by $H_t$ and $W_t$ by the tokens newly entering the cache at the provider's write price; $\rho_i = C^{\mathrm{logged}}_i / C^{\mathrm{ideal}}_i$ is how much more the run was billed than its prompts required
glossary.frontier step: a pair of adjacent runs on one benchmark's accuracy-cost Pareto frontier ordered by cost (35 steps over the card's seven benchmarks, 27 unresolved on accuracy)
glossary.paired-task bootstrap: resample the shared tasks with replacement and recompute the cost ratio of two runs; its 95% interval is the task-sampling uncertainty of a step's cost order, the scale against which the cache-plumbing term is judged

statement: On the HAL trace archives (379 archives, 262 runs in seven complete matrices, per-call token quadruples per card 2611.21515), compute for every run the realized hit share $h^{\mathrm{real}}_i$, the append-only bound $\bar h_i$ (step 0, token counts only) and the own-cache ideal $h^{\mathrm{ideal}}_i$ (step 1, from the logged message text with the provider's tokenizer), hence the cache-plumbing term $g_i$ and the re-pricing ratio $\rho_i$, tabulated by provider and by scaffold. Re-draw the seven frontiers at $C^{\mathrm{ideal}}$, count the frontier steps whose cost order flips, and set each flip against the paired-task bootstrap interval of that step's logged cost ratio. Random given: the logged $R_t$ is one draw from the provider's cache state at run time (the scaffold's breakpoint settings, the gap since the previous call, concurrent load); $h^{\mathrm{ideal}}_i$ is a property of the trajectory alone; $g_i$ is therefore a property of the (scaffold, provider, run-time) protocol and not of the agent, which is the claim's point.
claim: On the HAL leaderboard the cache-plumbing term reorders at least five of the 35 accuracy-cost frontier steps and spans more than a factor of two in billed cost across runs of one provider, so the cost axis ranks the scaffolds' cache handling as much as the agents' token use.
trick: Compare the cache hits the provider actually billed with the hits a token-exact cache would have given the same prompts, then re-draw the leaderboard's cost axis at the difference.
why_now: 2611.21515 (2026-11-16) re-priced every HAL run from its quadruples at one price sheet, found published costs up to 11.7x the reconstruction, and read the logged $R_t$ as given; 2611.22238 (2026-11-17) defined own-cache accounting and showed that server-reported hits warmed by sibling runs move one cost comparison from $+8\%$ to $+36\%$; HAL's released logs (2510.11977, 2025-10, 2.5B tokens) are the only cross-provider, cross-scaffold archive with provider-reported cache fields. title: The effective cache price: realized provider misses during tool waits and the sign of observation masking

glossary.observation masking: replacing old tool outputs in the prompt with a placeholder while keeping the latest $K$ (keep-ten: $K = 10$), the setting the card says Lindenbauer et al. recommend
glossary.cache-break term: editing the prompt at a position re-bills the suffix after it once at the uncached price, because a prefix cache serves only token-exact prefixes
glossary.break-even inequality: removing $B$ tokens pays when $R\,c\,B > (1-c)\,S$, with $R$ the remaining requests, $c$ the cached-token price relative to uncached, $S$ the suffix tokens recomputed once (card Eq. 2)
glossary.warm-cache crossover $c^*_0$: the list price below which rolling masking costs more than no management, $c^*_0 = (1+x)^{-1}$ with $x = \bar R / (K(1 + a/o))$, $\bar R$ the mean requests remaining when an observation is removed, $o$ the observation tokens, $a$ the reply tokens (card Eq. 3; measured 0.21 to 0.55 across the card's five models)
glossary.realized miss rate $m$: the token-weighted share of requests whose ideal hit (the append-only bound $\min(P_t, P_{t-1})$) is positive but whose provider-reported cache-read count is zero, so the whole prefix was re-billed at full price; the mechanism is the cache entry expiring in the gap before the request (a five-minute default time-to-live and inactivity eviction on the two price lists the card cites, stated from memory of those lists, to be verified at step 0)
glossary.inter-request gap $\\Delta\\tau_t$: wall-clock seconds between the end of call $t-1$ and the start of call $t$ of one run: tool execution, sandbox time, queueing
glossary.effective cache price $c_{\\mathrm{eff}}: $c + m(1-c)$, the expected price of a would-be-cached token once a share $m$ of requests miss entirely
glossary.crossover with misses $c^*_m$: with whole-request misses at rate $m$ independent of the edit, removal saves $B(c(1-m) + m)$ per remaining request and the cache break costs $(1-c)(1-m)S$ once, so removal pays when $$R\,B\,\bigl(c + m(1-c)\bigr) > (1-c)(1-m)\,S,$$ and the crossover becomes $$c^*_m = \frac{(1-m) - x\,m}{(1-m)(1+x)},$$ which equals $c^*_0$ at $m = 0$ and reaches zero at $m = c^*_0$: once the realized miss rate equals the warm-cache crossover, masking pays at every list price

statement: Step 0, on HAL's provider-billed traces (card 2611.21515: per-call quadruples; per-call timestamps assumed in the weave logs, verified first): on runs with caching active ($\sum_t R_t > 0$), compute the per-request miss indicator against the append-only bound, bin it by $\Delta\tau_t$, and report the token-weighted $m$ per benchmark and provider and the location of the step in the miss curve (expected at the provider's time-to-live). Step 1: put $m$ into $c^*_m$ with the card's $x$ per model and read the published masking results through it (the card's $+87\%$ to $+116\%$ at $c = 0.1$; the Complexity Trap's halving at API-returned, cache-priced cost and TokenPilot's provider-counted Keep-Last-N tables, both cited from this repo's C-W43-22 kill record): at $c = 0.1$ the miss rate that restores the saving is $m = 0.12$ for the card's most removal-friendly model ($c^*_0 = 0.21$) and $m = 0.50$ for its least ($c^*_0 = 0.55$). title: Cheap because it gives up: the failure premium inside the cost axis of agent leaderboards

glossary.cell $(i, j)$: one run $i$ on task $j$ with binary outcome $Y_{ij}$ and reconstructed cost $C_{ij}$ (card; 20,633 cells over seven benchmarks)
glossary.failure premium $\\phi$: the within-task cost ratio of a failed attempt to a successful one, $\phi = e^{-\beta}$ from the two-way fixed-effects fit $$\log C_{ij} = \alpha_i + \gamma_j + \beta\, Y_{ij} + \varepsilon_{ij},$$ with $\alpha_i$ the run effect (the agent's per-attempt efficiency) and $\gamma_j$ the task effect; standard errors clustered by task
glossary.cap-terminated cell: a cell whose run ended by the scaffold's step, token or time cap rather than by the agent submitting, read from the trace's step count against the scaffold's configured cap or from a logged termination reason
glossary.failure-share term of a frontier step: for adjacent frontier runs $i$ (cheaper) and $i'$, $$\Delta^{\mathrm{fail}}_{i i'} = \sum_j \bigl(Y_{i'j} - Y_{ij}\bigr)\bigl(c^{s}_j - c^{f}_j\bigr),$$ with $c^{s}_j$ and $c^{f}_j$ the task's mean successful and failed cell costs across all runs: the part of the step's cost gap that is the two runs' failure shares times the task's failure premium
glossary.efficiency term: the remainder of a step's cost gap after the failure-share term: tokens per attempt at matched outcome
glossary.frontier step: a pair of adjacent runs on one benchmark's accuracy-cost Pareto frontier ordered by cost (35 over seven benchmarks in the card)

title: Level or order: what each injected user-simulator fault does to the agent leaderboard the fidelity suites were built to protect

glossary.user simulator: an LLM that plays the human user against an agent so that sessions can be replayed and agents scored without people
glossary.fault (the paper's 'perturbation'): a known change to the simulator's profile, response instruction or turn budget; the paper injects ten (approve broken work, premature stop, front-loading, agent favoritism, profile artifact, adversarial goal, constraints removed, persona swap, co-debugger, language switch)
glossary.fidelity index: a score that says how much a simulated population or trace resembles real users (the paper's level 2 and 3; the SimulatorArena, VISTA and SWE-Together suites)
glossary.satisfaction total $s(x)$: per replay $x$, accepts plus stops minus corrects minus rejects as labelled by the Claude Sonnet 4.6 judge (the card's eq. 4); averaged over an agent's replays it is that agent's leaderboard score
glossary.level displacement $\\Delta_p(a)$: the change in agent $a$'s mean satisfaction under fault $p$: $\Delta_p(a) = \bar s^{C}(a) - \bar s^{p}(a)$, with $C$ the control replays
glossary.order displacement $\\tau_p$: Kendall's $\tau$ between the nine agents' ranking under control and under fault $p$; one swapped pair of nine agents moves $\tau$ by $2/36 = 0.056$
glossary.agent-uniform fault: a fault whose level displacement is the same offset for every agent, so the ranking and the standardized scores do not move
glossary.affine invariance: ranks and z-scores are unchanged when every agent's score is multiplied by a positive constant and shifted by a constant, $s \mapsto \alpha s + \beta$ with $\alpha > 0$; the paper's level-1 utility score is built from ranks ($S_{\mathrm{order}}$) and z-scores ($S_{\mathrm{gap}}$), so it cannot see an agent-uniform shift by construction
glossary.session bootstrap: resampling sessions with replacement, within agent, to put an interval on a per-agent mean or on $\tau$

title: Nine agents cannot order six simulators: the resolution of the leaderboard-agreement score in user-simulator meta-evaluation

glossary.level-1 utility score: the paper's leaderboard-agreement score for a simulator: $(S_{\mathrm{order}} + S_{\mathrm{gap}})/2$, with $S_{\mathrm{order}} = 100 \max(0, \tau)$ and $S_{\mathrm{gap}} = 100 \max(0, 1 - \mathrm{MAE}_z / (2/\sqrt{\pi}))$
glossary.Kendall's $\\tau$: rank agreement between the simulator's agent ranking and a reference ranking; at $n$ agents one swapped pair moves it by $2 / \binom{n}{2}$, which is 0.056 at $n = 9$
glossary.null standard deviation of $\\tau$: $\sigma_0 = \sqrt{2(2n + 5) / (9 n (n - 1))}$, the spread of $\tau$ between two independent rankings; 0.266 at $n = 9$
glossary.$\\mathrm{MAE}_z$: mean absolute difference between the simulator's and the reference's standardized per-agent satisfaction; $2/\sqrt{\pi} = 1.128$ is its expected value for two independent standard-normal vectors, so $S_{\mathrm{gap}} = 0$ is chance
glossary.sessions per agent: the paper's application scores nine agents on 351 sessions, about 39 per agent; the reference uses about 1,000 real sessions per agent
glossary.session bootstrap: resampling sessions with replacement within agent to put an interval on each simulator's $\tau$ and level-1 score
glossary.outranking probability: the share of bootstrap draws in which simulator $i$'s $\tau$ exceeds simulator $j$'s

statement: Step 0, analytic from the paper's printed numbers: at nine agents $\tau$ moves 0.056 per swapped pair and has null spread $\sigma_0 = 0.266$; the six simulators' $\tau$ span 0.44 to 0.67 (0.23, four pairs); backing out $S_{\mathrm{gap}}$ from level 1 and $\tau$ gives $\mathrm{MAE}_z$ of 0.60 (SimulatorArena, level 1 = 57) and 0.56 (Sonnet 5, level 1 = 47), both halfway between perfect (0) and chance (1.128). Step 1, on the released 351 sessions: a session bootstrap ($B = 2000$, within agent) of each simulator's $\tau$ and level-1 score against the fixed reference, and the pairwise outranking probabilities. Step 2: relabel the simulated turns with a second reaction judge (the reference stays with Claude Sonnet 4.6) and measure each simulator's $\tau$ shift against the 0.23 spread. Random given: the 351 sessions (about 39 per agent), each simulator's own sampling, and the judge's labels; the reference ranking is held fixed, and its own noise over about 1,000 sessions per agent is a second term reported separately if per-agent reference totals are released.
claim: At nine agents and about 39 sessions per agent, the leaderboard-agreement scores that order the six user simulators of 2611.24892 (Kendall's $\tau$ from 0.44 to 0.67) lie inside a single simulator's session-bootstrap 95% interval, so the suite's utility level does not order the simulators it compares.
trick: Count how many of the 36 agent pairs would have to swap to move one simulator's agreement score to another's, and ask whether 39 sessions per agent can pin a ranking that finely.

title: Where the forty turns go: a hindsight provenance count of forced rounds against the turn-cap depth of synthesized deep terminal tasks

glossary.depth $D$: the paper's measured depth: the smallest stated turn cap in $\{1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 40, 80\}$ under which one of two runs of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash or GLM-5.3-Flash passes the task in the terminus-2 harness
glossary.turn: one agent reply (a batch of shell commands $a_t$) plus the output $o_t$ the harness returns
glossary.key step: in the paper's generated tasks, a designed step per segment 'where the usual way of doing it goes wrong in this environment, with an error or silently, and only running the commands reveals it' (sec. 3.3); marked by comments in the reference solution so it 'can be removed mechanically' (App. F)
glossary.$K$: the number of designed key steps in a task, one per segment, so 3 to 6; the construction-time, model-free count of rounds the generator meant to force
glossary.newly-informed turn: a turn $t$ whose commands contain a string (a path, name, version, error token or value) that first appeared in $o_{t-1}$ and nowhere in the instruction, in $o_1, \dots, o_{t-2}$ or in $a_1, \dots, a_{t-1}$: a turn that could not have been batched into the previous one
glossary.$F(x)$: the count of newly-informed turns in run $x$; a hindsight, model-free reading of how many rounds the run drew on fresh information
glossary.retry turn: a turn that re-issues a command already issued earlier in the run, edited or not
glossary.forced-round budget $2K + 1$: the rounds a perfect agent needs if every key step costs one turn to hit the failure and one to apply the fix read from it, plus one opening turn; 7 to 13 for the paper's tasks
glossary.Cohen's kappa: chance-corrected agreement between two readers of the same items

statement: On the minimum-cap passing runs of the paper's 54 solved generated tasks (released, or regenerated with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in terminus-2 at cap $D$, about $1-2 per run), label every turn with a deterministic scanner as newly-informed, retry, or neither; compute $F(x)$ and the retry share per run, read $K$ per task from the key-step comments in the released reference solutions, and print $F$, $2K + 1$ and $D$ side by side; two readers hand-check 40 turns and report Cohen's kappa against the scanner. Step 2 runs the same scanner on the released uncapped runs of an audited shallow set (TMax's 88 Gemini runs, median 8 turns against median $D$ of 1). Random given: the run (one passing run at cap $D$, the model's own sampling at the paper's settings; the measuring model's temperature is not in the text and is read from the release); $F$ is a property of the run, $K$ of the task, and $D$ of the (task, model pair, harness) triple.
claim: In minimum-cap passing runs on the paper's generated tasks of median depth 40, fewer than one turn in three is newly informed by the previous output and the newly-informed count lies within a factor of 1.5 of $2K + 1$ (7 to 13 for six segments), so above a cap of ten the turn-cap depth counts the measuring model's retries, not rounds the task forces.
trick: Read each turn of a passing run, ask whether its commands use anything the previous output told it, count those turns, and compare the count with the turn cap the task was labelled with.
why_now: 2611.01927 (1 Nov 2026) is the first terminal-task set with a construction-time record of forced rounds (key-step comments, App. F; the verifier sees 598 of 604 key steps, Table 8) next to a measured depth, and its text leaves the gap between 3-6 designed key steps and $D \geq 40$ on 44 of 54 solved tasks uncounted ('waiting, reading and recovery', sec. 4.2); TMax (2606.23321) ships uncapped runs on the shallow comparator, and the paper's own hindsight read of its trajectories stops at a command-line ratio (1.06) and an output-token ratio (1.98, App. D).

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): data gate — the Code and Dataset links in the paper's header (URLs not in the text); confirm the released reference solutions carry the key-step comments and whether capped runs are released; if runs are not released, regenerate one passing run per solved task at cap $D$ with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in terminus-2 (54 runs, about 67,000 context tokens each at $0.30 / $1.20 per million, about $100). Step 1 ($0 compute, 3 days): the scanner (tokenize each command into identifiers, paths, numbers and flags; provenance check of each against the instruction, earlier outputs and earlier commands; retry detection by normalized command match), $F$, retry share and $K$ per task; the three-number table; kappa on 40 turns (20 scanner-positive, 20 negative). Step 2 ($0, 1 day): the scanner on TMax's released Gemini runs, $F$ against $N$ and $D$. Total: $0-100, 0 GPU-h, 6 days.
killing_experiment.dollars: $0 if the paper's runs are released; about $100 of API to regenerate 54 runs otherwise
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead if the median share of newly-informed turns is at least one half, or if $F$ exceeds $2K + 1$ by a factor of two or more on at least half the tasks while the retry share stays under 0.2: the turns beyond the designed key steps are then rounds that drew on fresh information — environment surprises the generator did not design — and $D$ is a task property on these tasks (the pre-registered alternative headline: synthesized depth comes from undesigned surprises, not from the key steps). Also dead if the scanner's kappa against the readers is under 0.6 (the ruler does not read provenance). Parked if neither runs nor reference solutions are released within 30 days (re-open trigger: the release; cost on re-open 4 days).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.5 that $F \leq 13$ at the median with a newly-informed share under one third and a retry share above 0.3 (the cheap models hit a key step's failure several times before reading the error correctly, and re-read truncated 10,000-byte outputs); 0.3 the alternative (newly-informed share at least one half, $F$ near $D / 2$, undesigned surprises dominate); 0.2 mixed across tasks. On TMax's uncapped runs: $F$ median 1-2 against $N$ median 8 (judgment 0.6), which would say the uncapped turn count the original papers report is reading and retrying, in the paper's favour.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The paper: 'Unlike the idealized $D^{*}$, $D$ depends on the models, the harness and the single state $e_0$, so it is an estimate rather than a bound' (sec. 2); 'a model that merges poorly overestimates the depth' (sec. 3.1); the gap on its own tasks attributed to waiting, reading and recovery without a count (sec. 4.2); the bias bounded from one side only — adding GLM-5.3-Flash lowers $D$ on 40 of 160 existing tasks, 32 by one cap (App. E.1); and the recommendation that 'builders of benchmarks and training data report depth alongside work' (sec. 5). The owners state the model dependence qualitatively and assume it is about one cap level; no sentence counts the forced rounds in a run.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the expected: the cap-depth ruler saturates — above $D = 10$ it reads the measuring model — so 'report depth alongside work' needs the provenance count or a strong merger, and the dataset label $D = 40$ means 'forty turns for a cheap model', while the paper's audit of existing sets (94% at $D \leq 3$) stands because it sits below the saturation point. If the alternative: the key-step design is not what makes synthesized tasks deep, the environment's undesigned surprises are, which rewrites the recipe (RST, FACET, this pipeline) for synthesizing depth.

title: Depth or count: SFT on synthesized deep terminal tasks against the same number of samples from the shallow sets it audited

glossary.SFT: supervised fine-tuning: training the model to reproduce recorded agent trajectories token by token
glossary.pass@1: the share of tasks a model passes in one run, averaged over runs
glossary.compaction-aware cut: the paper's sample boundary: a run is cut where terminus-2 would compress the context, and the next sample starts from the summary and the question-answer block (sec. 3.5, App. J)
glossary.sample: one training example: a segment of a passing run between cuts
glossary.deep arm: samples from passing runs on the paper's 105 generated tasks (median $D$ 40; $D \geq 10$ for all solved)
glossary.shallow arm: samples from passing runs on sampled TMax, SETA and RST tasks ($D \leq 3$ for 79-100% of solved tasks, median $W$ 25 to 119 lines)
glossary.matched quantity: the sample count (the paper's 4,941), with tokens per sample reported; a third arm matched on tokens if the deep arm's samples are longer by more than 1.5 times
glossary.run spread: the range of pass@1 over five independent evaluation runs of the same checkpoint

statement: Train Qwen3-8B (the paper's base, non-thinking) by SFT on two arms with the same open teachers (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash in terminus-2), the same compaction-aware cut and the same sample count: the deep arm from the paper's 105 tasks and the shallow arm from passing uncapped runs on sampled TMax, SETA and RST tasks; evaluate both arms and the base on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and OpenThoughts-TBLite with five runs per task and report pass@1 with the run spread, plus a token-matched third arm if the deep samples are longer by more than 1.5 times. Random given: one SFT seed per arm (the paper's regime), the evaluation sampling at a pinned temperature and harness (stated in the record; not in the paper's text), and the teachers' draws when generating the shallow arm; the measured quantity is a property of the (training set, sample count, base model) triple at 8B, and the headline names the scale.
claim: At a matched sample count and the same teachers, SFT on the paper's deep tasks ($D \geq 10$) gives Qwen3-8B no more than SFT on the shallow audited tasks ($D \leq 3$) on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and TBLite — within two points of pass@1, inside the five-run spread — so the reported gain is a sample-count effect and depth is not a training-data property at this scale.
trick: Train the same small model on the same number of trajectories from deep tasks and from shallow ones, and see whether the deep ones teach it more.
why_now: 2611.01927 (1 Nov 2026) ships the deep tasks, the SFT recipe and the compaction-aware cut with a gain of 2.6 to 4.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 3.4 to 9.1 on TBLite and no shallow control at equal count (the card: 'no comparison to SFT on an equal number of samples from the audited shallow datasets'); TMax, SETA and RST ship the shallow task files; the depth audit itself makes deep-versus-shallow at matched count the control nobody ran.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 2 days): data gate — the paper's 4,941 samples and SFT hyperparameters (unknown in the text); if unreleased, regenerate the deep arm with the two open teachers only (105 tasks, two uncapped runs each, about $1-2 per run, about $300) and accept a smaller deep arm (the paper used six teachers over 1,272 runs; DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash passes 40%, GLM-5.3-Flash 17%), matching the shallow arm to it. Step 2 (about 40 GPU-h, 4 days): two SFT runs of Qwen3-8B on about 5,000 samples (about 10 GPU-h each on one H100), then Terminal-Bench 2.1 and TBLite with five runs per task for three checkpoints on vLLM (about 20 GPU-h). title: Live at the boundary: a hindsight liveness ruler for compaction, read off CompAct-Bench's own remainders against its forward inventory

glossary.boundary $b$: the action index at which CompAct-Bench cuts a solved run and replaces the history before it with a summary
glossary.pre-boundary history $H_b$: the actions and observations $(a_1, o_1, \ldots, a_b, o_b)$ before the cut; the retained head (system prompt, task) is outside it
glossary.remainder: the reference run's own actions after the cut, $(a_{b+1}, \ldots, a_T)$, which the paper holds for every instance and never uses as a ruler
glossary.literal: a string the executor must reproduce exactly to act: a URL, a file path, an identifier of six or more characters, a number of three or more digits, a quoted string
glossary.live literal: a literal that first appears in $H_b$ (not in the head) and is used by a post-boundary action before any post-boundary observation re-supplies it; the compiler notion of liveness (a value is live at a program point when a later instruction reads it before it is overwritten) applied to a trajectory
glossary.live set $L_i$: the set of live literals of instance $i$, computed from the reference remainder
glossary.forward inventory: CompAct-Bench's Stage A list of about 27.9 'required' units per instance, written by GPT-5.6-Sol from $H_b$ alone (App. G.1)
glossary.dead unit: an inventory unit whose text carries no live literal
glossary.sufficient length $\\ell^\\star_i$: the character count of the minimal spans of $H_b$ (the line carrying each live literal) that together contain every live literal; a lower bound on how long a sufficient summary must be
glossary.live coverage $\\kappa_{i\\phi}$: $|L_i \cap M_b| / |L_i|$, the share of instance $i$'s live literals that appear verbatim in compactor $\phi$'s summary $M_b$
glossary.AUROC: the probability that a scored success outranks a scored failure under one predictor; 0.5 is chance

statement: On the released CompAct-Bench traces (200 reference runs with their remainders, 2,400 compacted contexts $M_b$, 7,200 continuations and the 200 forward inventories; the card names the project website and gives no release statement, so step 0 confirms what ships), extract with one regex extractor per literal class the live set $L_i$ of every instance from its reference remainder and compare it with the forward inventory: the share of inventory units that are dead, the share of live literals that sit in no inventory unit, and $\ell^\star_i$ against the paper's budget $0.10\,\ell(H_b)$. Then score every one of the 2,400 $(i, \phi)$ cells by live coverage $\kappa_{i\phi}$ and compare its AUROC for strict continuation success with the AUROC of the paper's own inventory-omission count on the same cells, task-stratified bootstrap. Random given what: $L_i$ is a property of the (task, reference run) pair at the executor's own setting (Claude Opus 4.8, high effort), one run per task; the three post-compaction continuations are not used to define liveness because they are conditioned on $M_b$.
claim: On CompAct-Bench's 200 instances the literals the reference remainder actually consumes sit in under a fifth of the forward inventory's 'required' units, and their coverage by $M_b$ predicts continuation success better than the inventory's omission count does.
trick: Read the run's own future, list the exact strings it reused from the cut history, and check how much of the benchmark's 'required' list those strings touch and whether keeping them is what predicted success.
why_now: CompAct-Bench v1 (2026-11-19) is the first corpus where a forward 'required' inventory, the compacted contexts, the continuations and the reference remainder sit side by side per instance, and its Case E discussion names 'the proportion of the history that was load-bearing' without computing it; the pipeline's own L4 records (CL-W43-05, CL-W44-06) show the harm side is occupied four times over (PRE/POST pairs, paired burden, rule compliance, policy sentences) while no fetched paper computes the need set from the remainder. Flag: release status unknown (the card: 'project website named (compaction-eval.github.io); release status unknown (not in text)').

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): open the project site; confirm the release carries (a) reference trajectories with remainders, (b) $M_b$ texts, (c) continuation traces with the strict-success flag, (d) inventories with unit text and the preserved/omitted/distorted judgments. Without (a) and (b) the probe is a sketch; the fallback is Compact-Bench 2610.31710's paired PRE/POST release (Coding only, recorded in this repo's CL-W43-05 kill record), where the full-history PRE continuation supplies the remainder. Step 1 ($0, 2 days): literal extractor (URL, path, identifier, long number, quoted string), precision checked by hand on 30 literals per domain; $L_i$ from the remainder with the head and post-boundary re-supply excluded; dead-unit share and out-of-inventory live share by substring match of literals into unit text; $\ell^\star_i / (0.10\,\ell(H_b))$ per instance. Step 2 ($0, 1 day): $\kappa_{i\phi}$ on 2,400 cells; AUROC for strict success per continuation and for Avg@3 > 0 per cell, against the inventory-omission count on the same cells; 1,000 task-stratified bootstrap resamples. Total $0, 0 GPU-hours, 4 days.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead if the inventory already is the need set: the dead-unit share is under 0.30 on both Search and Coding (over 70% of 'required' units carry a literal the remainder uses), or live coverage predicts strict success no better than the inventory-omission count (AUROC difference under 0.03 with the bootstrap interval covering zero) on both domains; then the ruler adds a regex to a list the paper already has. Dead at step 0 if the release lacks the remainders or the $M_b$ texts and Compact-Bench's release does not resolve literals per boundary.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.5 that the dead-unit share is at least 0.5 on Search and 0.6 on Coding (a remainder consumes a handful of URLs, entity names, file paths and line numbers; the inventory lists narrative units); 0.6 that $\ell^\star_i \leq 0.10\,\ell(H_b)$ in at least 70% of Search instances and 85% of Coding instances, so the 10% budget is not the binding constraint; 0.45 that AUROC($\kappa$) exceeds AUROC(omission count) by at least 0.05 on Search and by less on Coding, where Table 14 shows the repository re-supplies state (gain of $M_b$ at the early boundary $-2.7$ points).
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card's text: the inventory is 'the information required to continue the task', written 'from the original task and the complete pre-boundary history $H_b$, without access to any compacted context or continuation' (App. G.1); 'critical omission' is the leading label at '47.8% of early failures / 48.8% of budget exhaustions' and is scored against that inventory; the main setting is 'a 10% target retention ratio' (sec. 2.2) with no sufficiency reference; 'working-context compaction is inherently prospective' (sec. 4) is stated as a difficulty and never measured as the gap between forward and hindsight need.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If the dead share is high and $\ell^\star$ fits the budget: the omission rate compaction benchmarks report (25.3% of units omitted here) is measured against a ruler that is mostly dead weight, the scoring axis becomes hindsight-live coverage with a sufficiency-normalised ratio $r / r^\star_i$ where $r^\star_i = \ell^\star_i / \ell(H_b)$, and the loss is a selection failure under forward uncertainty, which argues for compactors that keep what the environment cannot re-supply (the sibling probe) rather than for larger budgets. If the live set exceeds the budget in most instances: the 10% ratio is the mechanism, the compactor ranking is a budget-fit ranking, and the benchmark should sweep $r$ around $r^\star$ with downstream runs, which its App. B.6 sweep did not do.

Who pays: compaction benchmark owners (CompAct-Bench, Compact-Bench, TRACE, ARCBench), harness teams choosing a compaction prompt and ratio, and anyone training a compactor (CompactionRL 2607.05378, ACON) who needs a target that is not a forward guess.

impact_ceiling.floor: A note with the dead-unit share, the $\ell^\star_i / 0.10\,\ell(H_b)$ distribution and the AUROC table on CompAct-Bench's release, cited by its v2 and by the next compaction benchmark. Requires steps 0-2. Judgment 0.55.
impact_ceiling.middle: Hindsight-live coverage adopted as a reported column by one compaction benchmark and a sufficiency-normalised ratio in one harness's evaluation; the 'critical omission' label split into live-and-dropped versus dead-and-dropped. Requires the sibling recoverability probe and a second corpus (Compact-Bench). Judgment 0.25.
impact_ceiling.ceiling: Liveness coverage becomes the standard scoring axis for compaction (every compaction paper reports it; compactor training targets it as reward). Requires a trained compactor from a group with compute and a second domain beyond coding and search. Judgment 0.08.

Pre-window precedents: live-variable analysis (Kildall 1973: a value is live when read later before being overwritten) and task-based extrinsic summary evaluation (Mani et al. 2002: score a summary by whether a downstream task can be done from it). Role words for the kill search: liveness, reachability, information need, sufficiency, oracle summary, minimal context, necessary context, task-relevant retention, prospective versus retrospective, dependency tracking, provenance, used by the continuation, context pruning oracle, upper-bound summary, hindsight. Lane rate per the CL-W44-06 record: about 2.6 papers per week.
scorecard.why_now: CompAct-Bench v1 2026-11-19 (inventory, $M_b$, continuations and remainder per instance in one corpus); App. F's environment-only arm (same date) for the sibling probe. Flag: release status unknown.
scorecard.register: Measurement with a scoring consequence (a hindsight-live column and a sufficiency-normalised ratio). It is not a compactor, not CompAct-Bench run on another benchmark, not a judge-based audit, and not a full-history control (occupied, CL-W44-06).

headline_test: What a compaction must keep is a fifth of what a forward reader says it must keep: compaction benchmarks score omission against the wrong ruler, and the 10% budget is not the binding constraint.

2610.31710 (Compact-Bench, the Coding fallback artifact per the CL-W43-05 record)
title: Dropped but re-fetchable: splitting compaction loss by whether the environment can give the literal back, with the paper's own no-history arm as the ruler

glossary.live literal: as in the sibling probe: a string from $H_b$ that a post-boundary action reuses verbatim (URL, path, identifier, long number, quoted string)
glossary.environment-only arm: CompAct-Bench's control (App. F, Table 14): the executor continues from the boundary state with neither $H_b$ nor $M_b$; run on Coding and Search
glossary.environment-recoverable literal: a live literal that at least one environment-only continuation of the same instance re-produces in its own post-boundary observations; the environment can give it back without the history
glossary.context-only literal: a live literal that no environment-only continuation re-produces; it lives only in the history
glossary.kept / recovered / guessed: for a continuation under $M_b$, a live literal is kept if it is in $M_b$, recovered if it is absent from $M_b$ and reappears in a post-boundary observation before its first use, guessed if it is used with neither (the executor reproduced it from nowhere, or from the head)
glossary.recovery cost $c_v$: the number of post-boundary actions from the boundary to the first observation that carries dropped literal $v$
glossary.kept-rate gap $\\Delta_\\phi$: $\kappa_\phi^{\mathrm{ctx}} - \kappa_\phi^{\mathrm{env}}$, compactor $\phi$'s kept rate on context-only live literals minus its kept rate on environment-recoverable ones
glossary.checkpoint-recompute trade-off: the systems rule for bounded memory (activation checkpointing, Chen et al. 2016): store what cannot be recomputed, recompute the rest; here store equals keep in $M_b$ and recompute equals re-fetch from the environment at cost $c_v$

statement: On the released CompAct-Bench traces, label every live literal of every Coding and Search instance as environment-recoverable or context-only using the paper's own environment-only continuations as the ruler, then measure for each of the twelve compactors the kept rate of each class in $M_b$ and the gap $\Delta_\phi$, and for each of the 7,200 continuations assign every live literal to kept, recovered at cost $c_v$, or guessed. Report, per compactor and domain, $\Delta_\phi$ with a task-stratified bootstrap interval, the share of Search live literals that are context-only, and the share of failed versus successful continuations that dropped at least one context-only live literal and never recovered it. Random given what: recoverability is a property of the (instance, boundary state, executor) triple at the executor's own setting, estimated from the environment-only runs the paper already made (one to three per instance; the count to confirm at step 0), so a literal re-found in one of them is recoverable and the rest are context-only under that sample, an upper envelope on 'context-only' that the record states.
claim: Frontier compactors keep a literal the environment cannot give back no more often than one a single re-read would restore: the kept-rate gap between context-only and environment-recoverable live literals is under 10 points for the top six CompAct-Bench compactors.
trick: Use the paper's no-history runs to mark which facts the environment hands back for free, then check whether the summarisers kept the facts that only the history held any more often than the free ones.
why_now: CompAct-Bench App. F (2026-11-19) is the first released no-history continuation at the same boundary states, which turns 'where state lives' from a domain label (Search versus Coding, Table 14) into a per-literal label at $0; harness practice already offloads state to files (context offloading) without any measurement of whether compactors select by re-derivability. Flag: release status unknown, and whether the no-history arm's traces are among what ships is the step-0 question.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): confirm the release carries the environment-only continuation traces for Coding and Search and the $M_b$ texts; without the environment-only traces the label needs about 400 own no-history continuations (200 instances, 2 each) at the executor's price, roughly $400 of API spend (inference) and 3 days, and the probe is reported above $0. Step 1 ($0, 2 days): live literals per instance from the reference remainder (the sibling probe's extractor); recoverability label from the environment-only traces; kept / recovered / guessed per continuation; $c_v$ for recovered literals. Step 2 ($0, 1 day): $\kappa_\phi^{\mathrm{ctx}}$, $\kappa_\phi^{\mathrm{env}}$, $\Delta_\phi$ per compactor and domain with 1,000 task-stratified bootstrap resamples; the dropped-never-recovered share among failed and successful continuations; the distribution of $c_v$ by domain. Total $0, 0 GPU-hours, 4 days, sharing step 1's extractor with the sibling probe.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead if $\Delta_\phi \geq 0.15$ with the bootstrap lower bound above 0.05 for at least four of the top six compactors on Search (compactors already select by recoverability; the recipe is in the models and the claim is false), or if context-only literals are under 30% of Search's live literals (the split has no leverage and the stage reversal is not about recoverability). Uninformative, and said so, if the environment-only traces are not released and the $400 own arm is not run.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.5 that $|\Delta_\phi| < 0.10$ for at least four of the top six compactors on Search (compactors select by narrative salience and recency, not by re-derivability); 0.6 that context-only literals are at least 60% of Search's live literals (URLs and entity names reached by a search chain the no-history executor does not repeat within budget) and at most 25% of Coding's (paths and symbols the repository holds); 0.5 that failed Search continuations carry a dropped-never-recovered context-only literal in at least 60% of cases against at most 30% of successes; 0.6 that the median $c_v$ on Search is at least three times the median on Coding, which is the stage reversal of Table 13 priced in actions.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: The card's text: the stage reversal is explained by where state lives at the domain level ('nine of the twelve compactors show a monotonic decrease on Search, whereas ten show a monotonic increase on Coding', sec. 3.3; the environment-only control, Table 14); the error labels are 'critical omission', 'progress/state loss', 'factual distortion' with no re-derivability axis (App. G); 'compaction can distort as well as omit task state' (sec. 1); what the compactor keeps is never measured against what the environment holds.
preregistered_surprise.belief_changing: If compactors are blind to recoverability: the compaction objective is mis-specified, the ratio and the omission count should be replaced by context-only coverage, and the cheapest recipe is a compactor instruction that ranks literals by re-derivability (the checkpoint rule: store what cannot be recomputed), testable by re-compacting the same histories and re-scoring kept rates. If compactors already prioritise context-only literals and Search still fails at 34.6% late: the loss sits in the guessed and distorted cells, which moves the lane from omission to distortion of kept literals, the direction CL-W44-06's occupants (lost binding) point.

Who pays: harness teams writing compaction prompts (what to keep), compaction benchmark owners (a recoverability axis beside omission), and training teams choosing a compactor reward.

impact_ceiling.ceiling: Re-derivability becomes a reported axis of compaction evaluation and a term of the compactor objective (store what cannot be recomputed), adopted by two benchmarks and one trained compactor. Requires a group with compute. Judgment 0.07.

title: Split by lot: whether a lead's document partition co-locates a planted conflict any better than a random split of the same documents among the same workers

glossary.planted pair $G_i = \\{A_i, B_i\\}$: the two conflicting values of one quantity the benchmark wrote into different documents of a task
glossary.Same / Split: the card paper's labels: both values read by one worker (Same) or only by the union of workers (Split)
glossary.realised partition $\\pi_e$: for Required execution $e$, the map from documents to the workers whose tool outputs contained them, read from the profiler's Source Reads stage
glossary.co-location $z_i$: $\mathbf{1}[\exists w : w \text{ read a document carrying } A_i \text{ and a document carrying } B_i]$, equal to the paper's Same label at Source Reads
glossary.pair completeness $PC$: the record-linkage term for the share of true matching pairs that a blocking step puts in the same block, so that they can be compared at all; here $PC = \frac{1}{N}\sum_i z_i$ over the pairs anyone read
glossary.blocking: in record linkage, partitioning records into blocks so only within-block pairs are compared; a pair split across blocks is never compared, whatever the comparator does; the lead's assignment of documents to workers is a blocking step
glossary.permutation null $\\mathbb{E}_{\\pi'}[PC: the pair completeness averaged over uniform random re-assignments $\pi'$ of the same documents (or the same directories) to the same number of workers with the same read-set sizes
glossary.hidden profile: the social-psychology paradigm (Stasser and Titus 1985) in which a group fails to pool information that only one member holds; the Split cell is a hidden profile created by the partition

statement: From the released profiler traces (step 0: the card says release status is unknown) or from own Required executions on planted-conflict document-review tasks (fallback), recover for each Required execution the realised partition $\pi_e$ and for each planted conflict the documents carrying $A_i$ and $B_i$, compute the observed pair completeness $PC_{\mathrm{obs}}$ (the paper's pooled value is 111 of 301 pairs read, 0.369), and compare it with the permutation null under two randomisations (directory-respecting and document-level) with 10,000 draws each, per model and pooled, with a permutation interval. Add the planting-design arithmetic: the Split share implied by the number of $A$- and $B$-directories and the worker count alone, against the observed 43.4% of 438. Random given what: $\pi_e$ is one draw of the lead's assignment policy at its default temperature; the null holds the worker count, the read-set sizes and the planting fixed and randomises only which documents went to whom, so the statistic isolates the lead's placement skill from everything else in the Required bundle.
claim: A lead that partitions documents without reading them co-locates a planted conflict at the rate a random split of the same documents among its workers would: the observed pair completeness is within 10 points of the permutation null.
trick: Shuffle which worker got which files, keep everything else, and see whether the lead's real assignment put the two conflicting numbers in one worker's hands any more often than the shuffle does.
why_now: 2611.22245 v2 (2026-11-18) is the first profiler that records per-worker read sets and planted-pair locations in one trace, which makes the null computable at $0 from data its authors hold; its Limitations ask for a run ('supplying identical evidence while varying which agents receive it') where a permutation test on the existing traces answers the narrower question first. Flag: release status unknown for the profiler, the traces and the Harvey LAB tasks (Grupen et al. 2026).

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): check the paper's release (code, profiler, traces) and the Harvey LAB tasks for public availability; without traces go to step 1b. Step 1 ($0, 2 days): parse per-worker read sets from Source Reads tool outputs (document identifiers), planted-document sets from the conflict specifications, $z_i$ and $PC_{\mathrm{obs}}$; 10,000 permutations under the directory-respecting and document-level nulls; per model and pooled, with the task-clustered permutation interval. title: Louder after the summary: whether routing an agent's own reads through a return-style summary raises the conflict flag rate per surviving pair

glossary.keep rate $\\kappa_S$: the probability that the summary carries both planted numbers given that the context it summarises carries both; string match on the paper's anchors
glossary.flag rate $s_X$: under arm $X$, the probability that the final report flags the planted conflict (the paper's two-criterion judge) given that the input the report was written from carries both numbers
glossary.arm R: the paper's own single-agent (None) report written from the raw context; observed: 71 flags on 220 contexts with both numbers, 0.32 (inference from Table 1 pooled rows)
glossary.arm S: the same model first writes a worker-style findings summary from its own raw context, then a fresh call writes the final report from that summary alone
glossary.arm SR: the summary prepended to the raw context; separates the salience of the summary from the removal of the raw reads
glossary.break-even keep rate $\\kappa^\\star$: $s_R / s_S$; above it a summary arm's net flag rate $\kappa_S s_S$ exceeds the raw arm's $s_R$
glossary.token distance $d_i$: the number of tokens between the first appearances of $A_i$ and $B_i$ in the raw context
glossary.judge-free flag proxy: both anchors within 300 characters of each other in the report plus one discrepancy cue word (inconsistent, conflict, discrepancy, differs, versus); calibrated against the judge on 40 items

statement: Take every single-agent (None) execution whose captured context carries both planted numbers (220 of 438 pooled observations, inference from Table 1; traces at step 0) and write the final report three ways from the identical context, R as the paper did, S through the model's own return-style summary, SR with the summary prepended, two samples per arm at the model's default temperature. Measure $\kappa_S$, $s_R$, $s_S$, $s_{SR}$ with the paper's judge rubric replicated on claude-sonnet-5 and with the judge-free proxy, task-clustered bootstrap over the 11 tasks, and the slope of $s_R$ and $s_S$ against $d_i$. Random given what: $s_X$ is a property of (model, context form) at the model's default temperature and the judge's; the context is held fixed across arms, so the contrast is the form of the input and nothing the agent did.
claim: On the same contexts holding both planted numbers, a report written through the agent's own return-style summary flags the conflict at least 15 points more often per surviving pair than a report written from the raw context, so the handoff summary is a salience filter whose net cost is decided by the keep rate alone.
trick: Hold the agent's reads fixed, write the report once from the raw pile and once from a short summary of the same pile, and count which one notices that two numbers disagree.
why_now: 2611.22245 sec. 4.4 (2026-11-18) is the first matched number in this direction, 72.2% against 33.3% flag rate when both numbers reach the lead through one contributor versus sit in one agent's raw context, read by its authors as provenance; the design guides argue full traces against condensed summaries (Yan 2025; Anthropic 2025a, 2025b per the card) with no per-pair salience term; the None contexts with both numbers exist in the authors' proxy captures. Flag: release status unknown.

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.45 that $s_S - s_R \geq 0.15$; 0.3 that the gain is between 0.05 and 0.15; 0.25 dead. Mechanism: a return summary enumerates figures into adjacent lines, collapsing the distance between the two values of one quantity from tens of thousands of tokens to a few lines; so $s_R$ falls with $d_i$ (negative slope, judgment 0.6) and $s_S$ does not, and $s_{SR} \approx s_S$ (the summary carries the gain, not the removal of the raw reads). title: The checker as the engine: the train-against / score-under 2x2 on RoboTwin 2.0's released and Verified success checkers

glossary.success checker: the hand-written function $c : \mathcal{S} \to \{0, 1\}$ a simulated benchmark evaluates on the simulator state to record an episode as a success; RoboTwin 2.0 ends the episode at the first state on which it returns 1
glossary.Verified checker: the card paper's repaired checker $c'$ for the same task: measures physical state instead of commanded values, keeps only conditions the instruction states, and requires the conditions to hold for one second; released with the paper
glossary.phantom success: an episode the released checker accepts and the Verified checker rejects ($c_e = 1$, $c'_e = 0$); 3.3-10.2% of the successes of the five imitation-trained RoboTwin policies in the card paper's Table 2
glossary.phantom share $\\mathrm{Phan}(\\pi)$: $|\{e : c_e = 1, c'_e = 0\}| / |\{e : c_e = 1\}|$ over a policy's episodes on a task set: the fraction of its credited successes that are phantom
glossary.optimised against a checker: a policy whose training signal was that checker's verdict on its own rollouts: on-policy RL with the verdict as reward, or rejection-sampling fine-tuning (RFT: behaviour cloning on the subset of its own rollouts the checker accepted)
glossary.imitation initialisation $\\pi_0$: the released checkpoint trained on the benchmark's expert demonstrations only (all 1,233 RoboTwin expert episodes pass the Verified checker, sec. 3.3, so this training signal is clean)
glossary.2x2 exploit interaction $X$: with $\pi_c$ and $\pi_{c'}$ optimised against $c$ and $c'$ from the same $\pi_0$ at the same episode budget, and $\mathrm{SR}_k(\pi)$ the success rate of $\pi$ scored by checker $k$ on paired seeds: $X = [\mathrm{SR}_{c'}(\pi_{c'}) - \mathrm{SR}_{c'}(\pi_c)] - [\mathrm{SR}_c(\pi_{c'}) - \mathrm{SR}_c(\pi_c)]$, what the Verified checker takes from the checker-trained policy beyond what it takes from any policy (the program note's $X$ with the checker in place of the solver budget)
glossary.phantom share of the gain $\\phi$: $\phi = 1 - \dfrac{\mathrm{SR}_{c'}(\pi_c) - \mathrm{SR}_{c'}(\pi_0)}{\mathrm{SR}_c(\pi_c) - \mathrm{SR}_c(\pi_0)}$: the fraction of the improvement a checker-trained policy reports under the released checker that disappears under the Verified one
glossary.defect tasks: the RoboTwin 2.0 tasks where the card paper's flips concentrate ('4 to 19 of the 50 tasks ... largely the same tasks for every policy', App. E), click bell and the press tasks first
glossary.paired seeds: the same initial-condition seeds for every policy and checker, so a difference between cells is a within-seed difference and its interval comes from the seed-level paired differences

statement: On RoboTwin 2.0's defect tasks, obtain a policy optimised against the released checker $c$ and its imitation initialisation $\pi_0$ (step 1: a released RL or RFT checkpoint whose reward was $c$; otherwise our own RFT arms $\pi_c$ and $\pi_{c'}$ from the same $\pi_0$ at matched episode and gradient budgets), roll every policy on the same seeds under the official protocol with $c$ and the released Verified checker $c'$ running side by side as observers and the episode continued past the first $c$ success (the card paper's own re-scoring protocol, sec. 4.4), and report $\mathrm{Phan}(\pi)$ per policy, the phantom share of the gain $\phi$, and the 2x2 interaction $X$ with paired-seed intervals. Random given what: outcomes are random given the seed through the policy's sampling noise at its released setting and the simulator's stepping; every cell uses the same seeds, so $\phi$ and $X$ are properties of (policy pair, checker pair, task set), not of the protocol. The scored object is the checker's verdict on visited states, so this is the lane's per-step audit with the checker in place of the solver, and the 2x2 is the operational test of exploitation the card paper states as an identifiability problem and leaves ('A policy that goes on to release is therefore credited early, and a policy that stops there is credited for a task it did not finish', App. C).
claim: On RoboTwin 2.0's defect tasks, a policy optimised against the released success checker earns at least a quarter of its reported gain over its imitation initialisation on phantom states that the Verified checker rejects.
trick: Train one policy against the benchmark's released success checker and one against the repaired checker, score both under both, and read the interaction as how much of the gain was the checker's bug.
why_now: 2611.25179 (2026-11-18) released, for the first time, a second scorer ($c'$) for benchmarks that policies are being RL-fine-tuned on, and measured phantom shares only for imitation-trained policies ('no policy is said to have been trained with the checker as reward', card); the RL-fine-tuning-of-VLA line of 2025-26 reports gains scored by the released checkers with no verified re-scoring (inference from the card's sec. 2 reading of the audit lineage; the kill search names the checkpoints); 2609.37771 (2026-09) showed checker fixes reverse method rankings in the acceleration setting. Flag: the enabling piece is a released artifact, not a technique.

killing_experiment.design: Step 0 ($0, 1 day): read the released Verified checkers and the re-scoring harness for RoboTwin 2.0; confirm the observer mode and the continuation past $t^\ast$; list the defect tasks from App. E and Table 4 (click bell and the press-without-contact tasks first, then the transient-success stack task); fix the task set (8 tasks) and seeds (official seeds, 100 per task) before any policy is run. Step 1 ($0, 2 days): census of released checkpoints on RoboTwin 2.0 / RoboCasa365 / RoboDojo whose training signal was the released checker (on-policy RL fine-tuning, RFT, DAgger with checker filtering) and whose imitation initialisation is also released; record for each the base model, reward, and episode budget. Step 2a (if a pair exists; about 20 GPU-h, $40, 3 days): roll $\pi_0$ and $\pi_c$ on the 8 tasks x 100 seeds under $c$ and $c'$ as observers; compute $\mathrm{Phan}$, $\phi$, and the lost/gained split per task with paired-seed 95% intervals. Step 2b (if no pair exists; 60-90 GPU-h, $120-200, 7 days): take $\pi_0$ = X-VLA or $\pi_{0.5}$ (Motus), the two with the largest click-bell phantom shares; run up to three rounds of RFT on the 8 tasks with 200 rollouts per task per round, one arm filtered by $c$ and one by $c'$, identical gradient steps and LoRA settings, two training seeds; evaluate all cells on the fixed 800 seeds under both observers; compute $X$, $\phi$ and $\mathrm{Phan}$ per round. The RFT null is weaker than an on-policy RL null and the record says so. Mechanism check in either branch: among $\pi_c$'s phantom successes, the distance from the end-effector to the bell at $t^\ast$ and the time to collapse of the stack, against $\pi_0$'s, so an amplified phantom share is tied to a named state, not a count.
killing_experiment.kills_if: Dead if, for a released on-policy RL checkpoint and its initialisation (step 2a), $\phi < 0.10$ and $\mathrm{Phan}(\pi_c) - \mathrm{Phan}(\pi_0)$ sits inside the paired 95% interval of zero on the defect tasks; in the RFT branch (step 2b), dead if after three rounds $X$ is inside the seed interval of zero and $\mathrm{Phan}(\pi_c)$ is within 2 points of $\mathrm{Phan}(\pi_{c'})$, recorded as a weaker kill. Parked at step 1 if no checker-trained checkpoint exists on an audited benchmark and the RFT branch cannot run under 90 GPU-h (trigger: the first released RL-fine-tuned checkpoint on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365 or RoboDojo). Uninformative, and said so, if the Verified checkers do not run as observers on the released RoboTwin 2.0 evaluation branch (step 0).

preregistered_surprise.expected: Judgment 0.45 that $\phi \geq 0.25$ with $\mathrm{Phan}(\pi_c) - \mathrm{Phan}(\pi_0) \geq 0.10$, concentrated on the press and stack tasks; mechanism: a terminal reward paid at the first accepting state makes the accepting-but-unfinished state the cheapest target (stopping within the 2 cm air gap removes a contact; a stack that stands for one physics step ends the episode before it falls), so the early-credit ambiguity of App. C becomes a gradient. Judgment 0.35 that $\phi < 0.10$: at these budgets the defect states are no nearer in policy space than the real completions, and the imitation prior holds. Judgment 0.20 in between. Secondary expectation: $\pi_{c'}$ matches $\pi_c$ under $c$ within 3 points (training against the repaired checker costs no credited success), so the interaction is carried by the $c'$ row.
preregistered_surprise.field_assumes: Two communities assume opposite things and neither has the number. title: Seeded faults for the fault-finder: the mutation score of an LLM checker audit by defect class, weighted by the verdict flips each class carries

glossary.mutation analysis: software testing's standard way to measure a test generator's recall when the true fault set is unknown: inject known faults ('mutants') into a correct program, run the generator, and report the fraction it catches (the 'mutation score'); a mutant that changes no reachable behaviour is 'equivalent' and is discarded before scoring
glossary.Verified checker $c'_j$: the card paper's repaired checker for task $j$, validated on 1,233 expert episodes and the 61 defect states (sec. 3.3); taken here as the correct program to mutate, since no other correct checker exists
glossary.defect class $k$: one of the card paper's five causes (Table 1): missing condition (17 of 61 defects), unstated requirement (15), proxy signal (16), loose geometry (10), transient success (3)
glossary.mutant $c'_{k,j}$: the Verified checker of task $j$ with one injected fault of class $k$: drop one stated condition; add one condition the instruction does not state; replace a measured physical quantity by its commanded value; widen one geometric tolerance by a factor of two; remove the one-second persistence window
glossary.reachable mutant: a mutant on which some state produced by the scripted expert or a released policy under physics gives $c'_{k,j} \neq c'_j$ — the card paper's own reachability rule ('teleport-only states are not counted', sec. 3.1) applied to the fault; unreachable mutants are equivalent and discarded
glossary.mutation score $m_k$: $m_k = \frac{1}{|M_k|} \sum_{(k,j) \in M_k} \mathbf{1}[\text{the audit's confirmed defect for } (k,j) \text{ names the injected condition or line}]$, over the set $M_k$ of reachable mutants of class $k$; a detection that names a different flaw does not count
glossary.flip-weighted recall $\\tilde m$: $\tilde m = \sum_k w_k m_k$ with $w_k$ the class's share of the verdict flips in the card paper's Table 4 (RoboTwin: transient success 50 of 205 flips from 1 audited defect; missing condition 18 of 205 from 10 defects), under the two class-to-repair-type mappings the card says do not reconcile
glossary.SimAudit: the released pipeline: an LLM reads instruction and checker code separately, proposes up to four disagreement states, a probe builds each under physics, a code-blind VLM reviews the frames; $0.78 in LLM calls and 18 minutes per task on average (App. D)
glossary.time-evolved fault: a fault whose trigger is a state that exists only after dynamics has run (a stack that passes at one step and falls within 60 ms; a gripper read as open on the first step after the command), as opposed to a fault readable from the code's conditions

statement: Take the released Verified checkers of 20 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, build 5 reachable mutants per task (one per defect class, reachability validated by a scripted-expert or released-policy rollout that changes the verdict), run the released SimAudit pipeline once on each mutant and once on each unmutated Verified checker, and report the mutation score $m_k$ per class with a Wilson 95% interval, the false-positive rate on the unmutated checkers, and the flip-weighted recall $\tilde m$ under both class mappings. Random given what: the audit's LLM and VLM run at their released sampling settings, so each $m_k$ is estimated from one pass and the pass-to-pass repeat on 20 mutants is reported as the audit's own floor (a second pass on the same mutant is the null for a one-pass miss). The quantity is a property of the audit pipeline on this benchmark's code and physics, not of the policies.
claim: A code-first audit of success checkers catches fewer than half of the injected faults whose trigger exists only in time-evolved physics, the fault class that one audited RoboTwin 2.0 defect turned into a quarter of all verdict flips.

glossary.paired protocol: RoboDyna runs each seeded episode twice, once with the simulator paused while the policy computes (synchronous, $\delta = 0$) and once with the scene advanced by the measured forward-pass time before the chunk executes (asynchronous, $\delta = 1$), and counts episodes whose binary outcome differs
glossary.seeded episode $i$: one task configuration and seed among the 700 non-hard matched pairs per policy (70 configurations x 10 seeds); the seed fixes the initial conditions and the scripted scene dynamics
glossary.outcome $g_i^a$: the binary success of seeded episode $i$ under arm $a$, read from the terminal simulator state
glossary.flip count $F(a, b)$: $F(a, b) = \sum_{i=1}^{700} \mathbf{1}[g_i^a \neq g_i^b]$, the number of matched episodes whose outcome differs between arms $a$ and $b$; RoboDyna's headline is $F(0, 1) = 85, 63, 34$ for $\pi_{0.5}$, X-VLA and FastWAM (Fig. 7)
glossary.same-arm repeat $0'$: a second synchronous run of the same 700 seeds with the policy's sampling noise redrawn; $F(0, 0')$ is the flip count with no latency at all. With $p_i$ the probability of success on seed $i$ under the synchronous protocol (random given the seed through the policy's sampling noise at its released setting and any simulator nondeterminism), $\mathbb{E}\,F(0, 0') = 2 \sum_i p_i (1 - p_i)$: the pure-error floor every cross-arm count must beat
glossary.fixed-delay arm $d$: the scene advanced by exactly $d$ physics steps of $4\,\mathrm{ms}$ before each chunk executes, regardless of the wall clock; $d \in \{1, 15, 27, 39, 59, 120\}$ is one physics step, one control tick ($60\,\mathrm{ms}$), the three measured mean latencies ($108$, $156$, $236\,\mathrm{ms}$) and twice the largest; hardware-independent by construction
glossary.control tick: RoboDyna holds each action for 15 physics steps, so the policy's command changes every $60\,\mathrm{ms}$ ($16.7\,\mathrm{Hz}$) at $250\,\mathrm{Hz}$ physics; an inference latency of $109\,\mathrm{ms}$ is 1.8 ticks and 3.6% of $\pi_{0.5}$'s 3.0-second chunk
glossary.excess flip share $\\xi(d)$: $\xi(d) = \dfrac{F(0, d) - \max\{F(0, 0'), F(0, 1)\}}{F(0, d)}$: the part of a delay's flip count that neither the repeat floor nor a one-step delay reproduces; the latency-attributable share
glossary.pure error (design of experiments): the variation measured by replicating the same design point; a treatment effect is tested against it, and without replicates lack of fit and noise cannot be told apart. The import: RoboDyna's two arms are two design points with no replicate; $F(0, 0')$ is the pure error
glossary.dose-response: $F(0, d)$ plotted against $d$; a latency effect proper rises with $d$ from the floor; a sensitivity-to-any-perturbation reading is flat from $d = 1$ onward
glossary.lost / gained split: $L(d) = \sum_i \mathbf{1}[g_i^0 = 1, g_i^d = 0]$ and $G(d) = \sum_i \mathbf{1}[g_i^0 = 0, g_i^d = 1]$, with $F = L + G$; the paper's mean difference is $(G - L)/700$ and hides both
